rules.sentence: Cavernous sinus syndrome results from obstruction, inflammation, or increased pressure within the cavernous sinus.
Common causes include thrombophlebitis, which can result from bacterial or fungal spread originating in the nasal mucosa, paranasal sinuses, or a skull fracture.
Thrombus formation can also occur in individuals with a hypercoagulable state, such as protein C or protein S deficiency, factor V Leiden mutation, or combined oral contraceptive use.
Tumors, such as a locally invasive pituitary adenoma, may also give rise to this syndrome.
